title.narrative: Guaranteeing the right to a sustainable and dignified city for favela communities in São Paulo

description.narrative:
Over 2 million people in São Paulo metropolitan area live in inadequate and unsafe housing on the furthest edges of the city in favelas (slums), far from jobs, services and without basic infrastructure, despite it being the richest city in L. America. High rents leave little for daily sustenance, whilst work travel of 4-5 hours/day leaves no time for family life. Historic legacies of slavery, internal displacement and contemporary discrimination mean black and mixed-race people are most affected by urban inequality. Violent disputes for territorial control between drug gangs and/or police and increasing impacts of climate change and environmental degradation leave communities vulnerable to tragedy. Nevertheless, Brazil has a strong policy-framework and technical capacity, which if applied and adequately resourced could turn cities like São Paulo into engines of socioeconomic inclusion, environmental transformation and equality. Strengthening the organisation, know-how and networks of communities to claim their rights is essential to bringing this about.
This project will enable greater accountability and responsiveness of public authorities at municipal and subnational level for the delivery of safe, secure and sustainable housing and urban services and reduction of environmental risks. This will be done through strengthening and consolidating the voice, influence and organisation of informal urban communities in 33 favelas on the periphery of eastern São Paulo. The project will benefit women, youth and older people from black and mixed-race communities with improved access to safe and permanent housing, land title, reductions in environmental risks, access to urban services, including sanitation, electricity, recycling and sustainable transport. Communities affected by insecure land tenure, eviction threat, inadequate and unsafe housing and neighbourhoods, lack of geographical mobility, violence and elevated exposure to environmental risks will be prioritised.
